score.note: First pass, evidence-grounded against games/gs1/asm/080e698c.s (never against the family-matcher's naive symbol-retargeted seed, which differs from this owner's real control flow entirely -- no per-member per-frame sprite loop at all). Started from 390 differing_halfwords / 230 wrong_instructions / 940 candidate bytes (owner is 944) and converged to the numbers above through four confirmed fixes: (1) the sine/cos-derived particle-velocity fields at frame==18 (`M2C_FIELD(particle,s32*,12)`/`+16`) need a SIGNED `s32 magnitude`, not `u32` -- the reference's `asrs r3,r3,#7`/`asrs r3,r3,#6` are arithmetic shifts and an unsigned multiplicand compiled to `lsrs`, a real value-changing bug for negative products; (2) the final particle-draw call's `(x>>16)-8`/`(y>>16)-8` arguments must be computed into named locals (`rx`/`ry`) BEFORE the `Func_080022fc` cell-index call, not inlined at the call site -- the reference computes both shifts immediately after the range guard, before touching `frame+i`; (3) the prologue statement order matters: `draw_destination = *cursor; extra_target = heap_cache[2];` must come BEFORE `M2C_FIELD(work,...,0x7828) = object;`, matching the reference's literal-pool/`ldmia` scheduling -- reversing this (moving the field store first) measurably regressed the score (263->446 dh) by knocking `work` off r9 onto fp entirely; (4) `new_x` (`member_a`'s field+8, later added to `dx_scaled`) must be pre-read into the `new_x` local itself and reused for the `dx` subtraction, rather than re-read fresh from `member_a` after the Func_080022ec call -- the reference caches this specific value into `sl` before the call (`mov sl,r2`) so it survives across it. Tried the identical treatment for the z-component (`new_z`/member_a field+16, dz computation): unlike x, caching z the same way made the allocator swap `work` from r9 onto fp function-wide (score regressed to 940 bytes/263 dh but 204 wrong_instructions, i.e. a differently-shaped, not simply worse, mismatch) -- reverted, leaving the z-component read fresh at point of use as before.
score.residual: The remaining diff is entirely register-allocation/scheduling noise, not a remaining algorithm, type, or call-argument mismatch: (a) the 1024-slot particle-lifetime-reset loop's counter lands in r3 here vs the reference's r8 (r8 needs the awkward `movs r4,#1; add r8,r4` two-instruction increment since Thumb high registers cannot take an immediate add, so the reference's choice is clearly a global allocation-pressure artifact, not a source hint); this single choice renumbers several downstream pseudo-registers for the rest of the function (member_b's z-field read order, several `mov rX,sl`/`mov rX,r8` register-name-only diffs at the Func_08009140/150/080 call trio, the final `pop {r0}; bx r0` vs `pop {r1}; bx r1`). (b) A handful of independent-immediate-load reorderings (e.g. `movs r1,#7; movs r2,#5` vs the reference's `r2` first then `r1`) that carry no value difference. Tried renaming/re-scoping the reset loop's counter (`i` vs a fresh `count`, block-scoped either way) and nesting `leftover` in its own block right at the sqrt call site: both zero effect, confirming these are compiler-internal tie-breaks rather than source-shape gaps reachable from this level. Did not chase further, per this family's already-documented pattern of this same residual class (games/gs1/recon/en/main/080e01e4.json note (b), 080d82b0.json, 080dc1ec.json).

rejected_experiments: Naively renaming the family-matcher's symbol-retargeted seed (out/family-transplants/main-080e698c/080e698c.c, the template's own body under this owner's name) was not attempted as a starting point beyond reading it for header/typedef/declaration scaffolding -- its body has no relationship to this owner's real control flow (no fixed 70-frame loop, no distance/velocity prologue, no wipe-in table-driven draw, no frame==18 particle spawn), confirmed directly against games/gs1/asm/080e698c.s from the start.

u32 magnitude for the frame==18 particle-spawn velocity fields (field+12/+16): compiled the sin/cos-scaled shift as logical (`lsrs`) instead of the reference's arithmetic (`asrs`) -- a genuine value bug for negative sin/cos products, not merely a byte-count regression. Fixed by declaring `s32 magnitude`.

Inlining `(x>>16)-8`/`(y>>16)-8` directly as Func_080072f4 (the r4-slot `_call_via_rN` veneer, modeled as the real DrawRectangleFn indirect call) draw-call arguments: this delays the two `asrs #16` shifts until right before the call, after the `Func_080022fc` cell-index call, which does not match the reference's placement (both shifts happen immediately after the `x<=0x7EFFFF && y>=0` guard). Fixed by hoisting `rx = x>>16; ry = y>>16;` into named locals before the cell computation.

Reordering the prologue so `M2C_FIELD(work,void**,0x7828) = object;` runs before `draw_destination = *cursor;` (matching a naive reading of where the reference loads the work+0x7828 constant relative to `sub sp,#36`): this knocked `work` off r9 entirely (onto fp) for the whole rest of the function and regressed differing_halfwords from 263 to 446. Reverted to the original heap_cache/cursor/draw_destination/extra_target/field-store/Func_080cd594 order shared with the other measured siblings in this family.

Caching member_a's field+16 (z-component) into `new_z` before the dz Func_080022ec call, mirroring the x-component fix that did help: this is a real reference-visible pattern (`mov r8,r0` right after the field+16 load) but adding it as a second new named local pushed the compiler's overall register count high enough to reassign `work` from r9 to fp, producing a differently-shaped 940-byte/263-dh/204-wrong_instructions candidate rather than a strict improvement. Reverted; only the x-component (`new_x`) is pre-cached.

Block-scoping `leftover` (the Func_080072ec r2-slot veneer's genuinely-unassigned second argument, matching the FixedSqrt `unused1`/`unused2` idiom from games/gs1/src/math/fixed_sqrt.c) into its own nested block immediately before the sqrt call, and separately renaming the particle-reset loop's counter from `i` to a fresh `count`: both changes were measured with zero effect on the score, confirming the residual register choices are not sensitive to declaration scope or identifier naming at this level.

Func_080072ec is the r2-slot `_call_via_rN` veneer at games/gs1/asm/080072e4.s (0x080072e4 + 4*2, i.e. `bx r2`). The retained assembly loads 0x030001D8 -- the same relocated IWRAM square-root routine used throughout the tree, per fixed_sqrt.c's veneer-audit comment -- into r2 immediately before the `bl`, so it is modeled as a direct call to the veneer's own symbol with the real jump target as a trailing argument, exactly as fixed_sqrt.c and battle_owner_52.c model their own r3-slot and r2-slot veneer calls respectively. The middle argument is never assigned between the preceding Func_080022ec call and this call in the retained assembly (no instruction touches r1 in between, i.e. it is genuinely whatever Func_080022ec's implementation leaves in r1), so it is passed as a deliberately-uninitialized local (`leftover`), matching FixedSqrt's own unused1/unused2 idiom for the identical situation.

Func_080e3980 is EffectPosition_ApplyAlternateStepAndYOffset per games/gs1/include/types.h (sibling of Func_080e3944 EffectPosition_ApplyBaseAndYOffset, used by the template and by 080dc1ec.c). Its first argument here is read from target+8 as a plain s32 -- the exact same field used directly as Func_080b5098's member-id argument earlier in this same owner -- so it is modeled as taking a member id, not a position-record pointer, unlike Func_080e3944's (src,dest) shape.

Field offsets on `member_a` (0x28/0x2C-unused/0x30/0x34/0x44/0x48/0x58/0x5A) are read directly from the retained assembly and are not otherwise documented in this family; they are consumed exclusively by the generic Object_ResetMotion/SetPosition/SetMode trio immediately afterward, so no more specific struct/field names are claimed than the raw offsets.

Semantic summary: a camera-tracking / wipe-in battle intro effect. Loads a palette and sets BG2 scale, registers three effect callbacks (0x73 against extra_target, 0x61 against work, 0x6D against work+0x3E80), resolves one draw-callback pair via Func_080cef64, clears a 1024-slot particle pool, then computes the on-screen distance between two specific tracked party members (ids at target+8 and (s16)target+36) and uses it to set the first member's velocity/position via the generic object-motion API. Runs a fixed 70-frame loop: every frame re-projects the tracked member (Func_080e3980) to drive a BG affine register and, during frames 8-23, draws a wipe-in decorative rectangle from a small 7-entry table family (selected by a facing/variant flag at target+4); at frame 18 exactly it spawns 16 fresh randomized-velocity particles into the pool; every frame it also ages and draws all 128 active particles in that pool's first slice.

Cross-edition relocation-aware verification on 2026-08-31 locates this owner in all six releases and proves all 706 non-relocation core bytes identical. The object symbol covers 942 bytes; the classified 944-byte retained extent includes its two-byte trailing alignment.

A shipped compiler-route and pass sweep tested routed GCC 2.96, explicit GCC 2.96, old-agbcc, regmove, both schedulers, CSE follow/skip blocks, GCSE, expensive optimizations, thread jumps, strength reduction, and rerun-CSE-after-loop. Canonical and most pass toggles remain at the exact 944-byte extent and 294 differing halfwords; all alternatives either tie or regress.

The complete semantic audit, exact retained extent, equal branch topology, six-edition core identity, and bounded source/route probes satisfy the battle_effect_compiler_allocation_module gate. The remaining differences are the already-recorded reciprocal register roles and independent scheduling choices; the retained assembly is Proven ASM while this C remains its evidence-bearing reconstruction.
